summary.narrative:
Riverstone Commons' decarbonization package converts central gas boilers to air-source heat pumps across all four buildings, adds a 180 kW rooftop solar array, and completes an envelope air-sealing pass on the two oldest buildings. The package was selected from Soapbox's decarb-plan engagement following measure-level economic screening; this report reflects the final, already-decided scope — no further option analysis is presented.

The combined package reduces site emissions by an estimated 38% against baseline and pays back in just over six years on a net-of-incentive basis, driven primarily by IRA Section 48 solar ITC and the local utility's heat pump rebate program.

implementation.narrative: Phased across two construction seasons to avoid displacing residents during heating-system cutover. Heat pump conversion in Buildings A and B is sequenced first (spring 2027) to validate performance before committing Buildings C and D.

considerations.title: Tenant coordination
considerations.detail: Heat pump cutover requires 2-3 day unit access windows per building; coordinate with property management's existing turnover schedule to minimize occupied-unit disruption.

considerations.title: Utility interconnection
considerations.detail: Solar array requires utility interconnection approval — submit application at least 6 months ahead of the planned install window given the local utility's current queue.

considerations.title: Incentive timing
considerations.detail: IRA Section 48 ITC and the heat pump rebate both require equipment to be placed in service within the program's current funding cycle — confirm install schedule against program deadlines before finalizing contractor bids.

incentive_programs.summary: Programs identified below are stackable with the IRA Section 48 ITC and heat pump rebate already reflected in the financial figures.
